title: Local-marginal spectral-window transfer
question: Does taking the local partial trace of a finite-volume Gibbs state before applying a fixed local spectral window produce a volume-stable kinetic corridor and an auditable boundary/complement split?

model.route_split: local marginal first, then spectral window; the complement is Q_{U,E} rho_{V,U} Q_{U,E}
model.analytic_target: derive a boundary-conditioned local Gibbs tail and a cutoff-independent form-core transfer without global partition-ratio volume loss

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks the scalar exponential tail term and finite split/scope identities; partial traces, spectra, matrices and QFT limits remain Python/open analysis.

qft_interface.closed: On the finite declared grid, local reduction before projection gives an exact trace-duality check and a volume-stable fixed-window corridor for the sampled local kinetic target.
qft_interface.open: The boundary-conditioned Gibbs-tail theorem, cutoff-independent common core, beta/eta independence, all source/volume/shape uniformity, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite local-marginal interface only; no physical-sector conclusion or production-owner transfer is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite local-marginal spectral-window transfer stress only. It proves no cutoff- or volume-uniform Gibbs complement bound, no beta/eta-independent topology, no domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: Local marginal stability separates the global volume trace from a local spectral complement, but it cannot replace a boundary-conditioned uniform tail theorem or the invariant common-core transfer.
